title: He held the bag.
paragraphs:
He held the bag.
She broke the jar.
And only one of them walked away remembered for love.
Because proximity to Jesus does not equal surrender to Jesus.
Read that again.

Judas was close enough to hear every sermon…
close enough to see every miracle…
close enough to hold the ministry finances—
—and still far enough to betray Him for silver.

Mary, on the other hand, didn’t hold position.
She held nothing back.
And that’s where the tension lives.
Because some of us look more like Judas than we dare admit.

Not in public.
But in private.

We don’t kiss Jesus to betray Him—
we just delay obedience…
justify compromise…
and quietly take what was never ours.
John 12:4–6 exposes something uncomfortable: Judas criticized Mary’s worship, pretending to care for the poor, but Scripture reveals his heart—he was stealing from the money bag.
That means this:

You can sound spiritual…
and still be hiding sin.

You can criticize devotion…
while secretly feeding your flesh.

You can stand near Jesus…
and still love something more than Him.
Let that sit.
Where are you “holding the bag” in your life?
Where are you taking instead of surrendering?

Mary walks in—no speech, no announcement—just surrender.
She breaks the alabaster jar, something costly, something personal, something she could never take back.
John 12:3 says the fragrance filled the house.
What she poured out publicly revealed what she treasured privately.
AHA REVELATION:
What you worship will always be exposed by what you’re willing to lose.

Judas saw waste.
Jesus saw worship.
And here’s the mirror—
SPIRITUAL MIRROR STATEMENT:
If your sacrifice feels “too much,” maybe your love hasn’t gone deep enough yet.
Because this is where it cuts deeper.

Some of us aren’t rejecting Jesus outright—
we’re just managing Him.

Keeping Him close enough for comfort…
but not close enough to confront us.

We sing, we serve, we show up—
but there’s still a hidden drawer in our heart labeled “mine.”

A relationship.
A habit.
A secret thought life.
A delayed “yes.”
And we guard it like Judas guarded that bag.

But Ecclesiastes 5:10 whispers a warning: “Whoever loves money never has enough…”
Because what you refuse to surrender will eventually own you.
Conviction hits here—

You don’t lose your soul in one moment.
You drift there in small compromises.

Judas didn’t wake up and decide to betray Jesus.
He slowly chose lesser loves—again and again—until 30 pieces of silver felt worth it.
And some scholars interpret that Judas may have expected Jesus to establish an earthly kingdom—when Jesus didn’t meet his expectation, disappointment turned into betrayal.
That’s dangerous.
Because unmet expectations can become open doors for hidden rebellion.
But here’s where grace interrupts the story.

Because while Judas was taking—
Jesus was already giving.

Giving His time.
Giving His truth.
Giving His life.
And eventually—giving His blood.
Romans 5:8 declares it plainly: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

Not after we fixed ourselves.
Not after we stopped stealing, hiding, pretending.
While we were still Judas-hearted.

The Gospel is not behavior management.
It is heart transformation.

Jesus didn’t come to polish your image.
He came to break your chains.

Sin is real.
And it separates us from God (Romans 3:23).
But grace is louder.

At the cross, Jesus took the betrayal, the greed, the hidden sin—
and paid for it in full.
And when He rose again, He made this possible:

A thief can become a worshiper.
A taker can become a giver.
A hidden sinner can become a surrendered son or daughter.
IDENTITY SHIFT:

You are not called to manage sin.
You are called to die to it—and live in Christ.

You are not a slave to what you’ve been hiding.
In Jesus, you are free to become who you were meant to be.
But here’s the invitation—
Break the jar.

Not halfway.
Not later.
Now.

Lay down the thing you keep excusing.
Release the control you keep gripping.
Stop negotiating with what Jesus already paid to remove.
Because Luke 9:23 says if anyone would come after Him, he must deny himself, take up his cross daily, and follow.
Daily.
Not selectively.
And yes—it will cost you.
But nothing you surrender compares to what you gain in Christ.

The peace.
The freedom.
The clean heart.
The restored intimacy.

If this is hitting you deeper than expected…
it’s not coincidence.
It’s conviction wrapped in grace.
Not for information—but for transformation.
If your spirit is hungry, stay close.
Right now—
Choose.

Not emotionally.
Not temporarily.
Decisively.

Are you holding the bag—
or breaking the jar?
And next—there’s something even deeper about the kiss of Judas most people miss.
